title: Duality reciprocity
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$; let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and for
$P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$ write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for coefficientwise extension.
Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth,
proper, and geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, let $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $F$ be the
geometric Frobenius. Fix an indeterminate
$T$. For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, put
$V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$, where $H^i(X,\Ql)$ denotes the
ordinary cohomology group,
and set $P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF\mid V_{i,\ell})$. Let
$P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be the
normalized integral factor
with $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$; these determinant data are the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Put
$b_i=\deg P_i$, and set

$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T).
$$

Let $\langle-,-\rangle_i$ be the
trace–cup-product pairing. Poincare
duality identifies
the multiset of
Frobenius eigenvalues in degree $2d-i$ with

$$
\left\{\frac{q^d}{\alpha}:\alpha
\text{ is an eigenvalue in degree }i\right\},
$$

including algebraic multiplicity. Moreover,

$$
b_i=b_{2d-i},
\qquad
D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i},
$$

and the integral factors satisfy the Laurent-polynomial identity

$$
P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T)
\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}].
$$

For the middle degree $i=d$, the pairing is $(-1)^d$-symmetric. In particular,
if $d$ is odd, then $b_d$ is even.

proof.text: *Step 1 (the spaces, the Betti numbers, and the eigenvalue multisets).* Fix $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ and write $V_j=V_{j,\ell}=H^j(X,\Ql)$ and $F_j=F_{j,\ell}=F|_{V_j}$ for the members of the smooth-proper cohomological family [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]; each $V_j$ is a finite-dimensional $\Ql$-vector space by [prop-cohomological-finiteness], and $P_{j,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_j\mid V_j)\in\Ql[T]$. By [def-weil-betti-numbers] and [def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor], $P_j\in\mathbf Z[T]$ is the polynomial with $P_j(0)=1$ and $P_j^{(\ell)}=P_{j,\ell}$ (unique by [prop-integral-recovery]), $b_j=\deg P_j$, and the last clause of [prop-integral-recovery] gives $b_j=\deg P_j=\dim_{\Ql}V_j$. Let $\Qlb$ be the algebraic closure of $\Ql$ chosen in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. By [lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization] applied to $P_{j,\ell}$ (which has $P_{j,\ell}(0)=1$), there are $\alpha_{j,1},\ldots,\alpha_{j,n_j}\in\Qlb^\times$, $n_j=\deg P_{j,\ell}=\deg P_j=b_j$ (the coefficientwise extension $\mathbf Z[T]\to\Ql[T]$ preserves degrees, [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-degree] with [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero]), with $P_{j,\ell}(T)=\prod_{r=1}^{b_j}(1-\alpha_{j,r}T)$ in $\Qlb[T]$, and the $\alpha_{j,r}$ are the reciprocal roots of $P_{j,\ell}$ counted with algebraic multiplicity [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots]; by [prop-weil-reciprocal-roots-eigenvalues] they are exactly the eigenvalues of $F_j$ on $V_j\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb$ counted with algebraic multiplicity. This multiset $\{\alpha_{j,1},\ldots,\alpha_{j,b_j}\}$ is what the statement calls the multiset of Frobenius eigenvalues in degree $j$.

source.place: ## Proof, step 1, first sentence ('let $\alpha_{i,1},\ldots,\alpha_{i,n_i}$ denote the eigenvalues of $F$ on $V_i$, counted with algebraic multiplicity') and step 2 ('$b_j=\dim V_j=n_j$', 'the factorization $P_i(T)=\prod(1-\alpha_{i,r}T)$'); the identification of eigenvalues with reciprocal roots, and $b_j=\dim V_j$, are taken there without argument

proof.text: *Step 2 (the $\Ql$-valued similitude pairing).* By [prop-poincare-pairing], the trace–cup-product pairing $\langle-,-\rangle_i:V_i\times V_{2d-i}\to\Ql(-d)$ of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup] is perfect (both induced maps $V_i\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ql}(V_{2d-i},\Ql(-d))$ and $V_{2d-i}\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ql}(V_i,\Ql(-d))$ are bijective), and $\langle Fx,Fy\rangle_i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle_i$ for all $x\in V_i$, $y\in V_{2d-i}$, geometric Frobenius acting on $\Ql(-d)$ by $q^d$ [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. The value space $\Ql(-d)$ is the Tate twist of degree $-d$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], a one-dimensional $\Ql$-vector space (the twist of degree $1$ has rank one and $\Lambda(-d)=\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda(d),\Lambda)$). Choose a $\Ql$-linear isomorphism $\tau:\Ql(-d)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Ql$ and put $\beta_i=\tau\circ\langle-,-\rangle_i:V_i\times V_{2d-i}\to\Ql$. Then $\beta_i$ is $\Ql$-bilinear; it is perfect, because composing with the isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ql}(-,\Ql(-d))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ql}(-,\Ql)$, $\varphi\mapsto\tau\circ\varphi$, carries the two induced maps of $\langle-,-\rangle_i$ to those of $\beta_i$; and $\beta_i(F_ix,F_{2d-i}y)=\tau(q^d\langle x,y\rangle_i)=q^d\beta_i(x,y)$. Finally $q^d\neq0$ in $\Ql$, since $\mathbf Z\to\Ql$ is injective [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero]. So $(F_i,F_{2d-i})$ is a similitude pair with multiplier $c=q^d\in\Ql^\times$ for the perfect pairing $\beta_i$, in the sense of [lem-weil-similitude-pairing-reciprocity].

source.place: Chapter II, §27, proof of Theorem 27.12, p. 158 (the pairing $H^{2d-r}(X,\Ql)\times H^r(X,\Ql(d))\to H^{2d}(X,\Ql)\to\Ql$ and its Frobenius compatibility $\eta_X(F_*x\cup x')=\eta_X(x\cup F^*x')$, with $F_*F^*=q^d$ from Remark 27.4(a), p. 155); here in the form of [prop-poincare-pairing], whose similitude $\langle Fx,Fy\rangle_i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle_i$ replaces Milne's $F_*=q^d/F^*$. The trivialization of $\Ql(-d)$ is the blueprint's step 4 ('choose a nonzero $\Ql$-linear trivialization $\Ql(-d)\simeq\Ql$')

proof.text:
*Step 3 (the eigenvalue multiset in degree $2d-i$, and $b_i=b_{2d-i}$).* Apply [lem-weil-similitude-pairing-reciprocity] with $K=\Ql$, $V=V_i$, $W=V_{2d-i}$, $\beta=\beta_i$, $F=F_i$, $G=F_{2d-i}$, $c=q^d$ (hypotheses from Step 2), and $\iota:\Ql\hookrightarrow\Qlb$ the inclusion. Its clause 1 gives $\dim_{\Ql}V_{2d-i}=\dim_{\Ql}V_i$, hence, by Step 1, $b_{2d-i}=\dim V_{2d-i}=\dim V_i=b_i$. Its clause 4 gives that the multiset of reciprocal roots of $P_{2d-i,\ell}=\det(1-TF_{2d-i}\mid V_{2d-i})$ in $\Qlb$ is the image of the multiset of reciprocal roots of $P_{i,\ell}$ under $\alpha\mapsto q^d/\alpha$, with multiplicities; in the notation of Step 1,

$$
\{\alpha_{2d-i,1},\ldots,\alpha_{2d-i,b_{2d-i}}\}=\{q^d/\alpha_{i,1},\ldots,q^d/\alpha_{i,b_i}\},
\qquad
P_{2d-i,\ell}(T)=\prod_{r=1}^{b_i}\bigl(1-q^d\alpha_{i,r}^{-1}T\bigr)\ \text{in }\Qlb[T].
$$

By Step 1 both multisets are the multisets of Frobenius eigenvalues, with algebraic multiplicity, in degrees $2d-i$ and $i$: this is the first assertion of the proposition.

source.place: Chapter II, §27, proof of Theorem 27.12, p. 158: 'the eigenvalues of $F^*$ acting on $H^r(X)$ are the same as the eigenvalues of $F_*$ acting on $H^{2d-r}(X)$. But $F_*=q^d/F^*$ (see 27.4a), and so if $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s$ are the eigenvalues of $F^*$ acting on $H^r(X,\Ql)$, then $q^d/\alpha_1,\ldots,q^d/\alpha_s$ are the eigenvalues of $F^*$ acting on $H^{2d-r}(X,\Ql)$'; the linear algebra Milne leaves implicit is [lem-weil-similitude-pairing-reciprocity]. Blueprint: ## Proof, step 1 (the display of the two multisets) and step 2 ('$b_{2d-i}=b_i$')

proof.text: *Step 4 (the product rule $D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i}$).* By [def-weil-determinant-constants], $D_j=(-1)^{b_j}[T^{b_j}]P_j(T)\in\mathbf Z\setminus\{0\}$ and the image of $D_j$ in $\Ql$ is $\det(F_j\mid V_j)$, for $j=i$ and $j=2d-i$. Clause 2 of [lem-weil-similitude-pairing-reciprocity], applied as in Step 3, gives $\det(F_i\mid V_i)\cdot\det(F_{2d-i}\mid V_{2d-i})=(q^d)^{\dim V_i}=q^{db_i}$ in $\Ql$ (Step 1: $\dim V_i=b_i$). Hence the integers $D_iD_{2d-i}$ and $q^{db_i}$ have the same image in $\Ql$, and since $\mathbf Z\to\Ql$ is injective [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero], $D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i}$ in $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: ## Proof, step 2: '$D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T)=\prod\alpha_{i,r}$', '$D_{2d-i}=\prod q^d/\alpha_{i,r}=q^{db_i}/D_i$, and hence $D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i}$'; the blueprint computes with the eigenvalue products, here the product rule is clause 2 of [lem-weil-similitude-pairing-reciprocity] (the determinant is the product of the eigenvalues), and the descent from $\Ql$ to $\mathbf Z$, which the blueprint omits, is written out

proof.text:
*Step 5 (the Laurent-polynomial identity).* Work first in $\Qlb[T,T^{-1}]$ [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-reciprocal-roots-laurent-identity] with $L=\Qlb$, $P=P_{2d-i,\ell}$, $Q=P_{i,\ell}$ (both have constant coefficient $1$, [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]) and $c=q^d\in\Qlb^\times$. Its hypothesis holds: by Step 3 the reciprocal roots of $P_{2d-i,\ell}$ are the $q^d/\alpha_{i,r}$, so the reciprocal roots of $Q=P_{i,\ell}$, namely the $\alpha_{i,r}=q^d/(q^d/\alpha_{i,r})$, are the images of those of $P=P_{2d-i,\ell}$ under $\alpha\mapsto c/\alpha$, with multiplicities ($\alpha\mapsto q^d/\alpha$ is an involution of $\Qlb^\times$); and $n=\deg P_{2d-i,\ell}=b_{2d-i}=b_i$ (Step 1 and Step 3). The lemma's determinant constant of $Q=P_{i,\ell}$ is $D_Q=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_{i,\ell}$, which is the image in $\Ql$ of $D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i$, because the coefficientwise extension $P_i\mapsto P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ preserves every coefficient [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-degree] ([def-weil-coefficientwise-extension], [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient]). Clause 2 of the lemma therefore gives, in $\Qlb[T,T^{-1}]$,

$$
P_{2d-i,\ell}(q^{-d}T^{-1})=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_{i,\ell}(T).
$$

Now descend to $\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}]$. Both sides are the images, under the coefficientwise map $\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}]\to\Qlb[T,T^{-1}]$ induced by the field inclusions $\mathbf Q\subset\Ql\subset\Qlb$ (the unique ring homomorphism $\mathbf Q\to\Ql$ extending $\mathbf Z\to\Ql$; it is injective, as is every ring homomorphism out of a field), of the elements $P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})$ and $(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T)$ of $\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}]$: indeed $P_j^{(\ell)}=P_{j,\ell}$, the coefficientwise map is a ring homomorphism [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective] commuting with the substitution $T\mapsto q^{-d}T^{-1}$ of [def-weil-rational-function-field] ([def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring]), and $D_i\in\mathbf Z\setminus\{0\}$ is invertible in $\mathbf Q$. The coefficientwise map $\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}]\to\Qlb[T,T^{-1}]$ is injective ([def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring]; a Laurent polynomial is determined by its coefficients and $\mathbf Q\to\Qlb$ is injective, [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero]). Hence

$$
P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T)\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}],
$$

which is the Laurent-polynomial identity of the proposition.

source.place: ## Proof, step 3: '$P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})=\prod(1-\alpha_{i,r}^{-1}T^{-1})=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}(\prod\alpha_{i,r})^{-1}\prod(1-\alpha_{i,r}T)=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T)$'; the computation is [lem-weil-reciprocal-roots-laurent-identity], and the passage from $\Qlb[T,T^{-1}]$, where the factorization lives, to $\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}]$, which the blueprint does not mention, is written out

proof.text: *Step 6 (middle degree: $(-1)^d$-symmetry and the parity of $b_d$).* By the graded-commutativity clause of [prop-poincare-pairing], $\langle y,x\rangle_{2d-i}=(-1)^i\langle x,y\rangle_i$ for $x\in V_i$, $y\in V_{2d-i}$; for $i=d$ this reads $\langle y,x\rangle_d=(-1)^d\langle x,y\rangle_d$ for all $x,y\in V_d$, i.e. the middle pairing is $(-1)^d$-symmetric. Suppose $d$ is odd. The $\Ql$-valued pairing $\beta_d=\tau\circ\langle-,-\rangle_d:V_d\times V_d\to\Ql$ of Step 2 (with $i=d$) is bilinear and perfect, hence nondegenerate ($\beta_d(x,-)=0$ forces $x=0$ by the bijectivity of $x\mapsto\beta_d(x,-)$), and satisfies $\beta_d(y,x)=-\beta_d(x,y)$. Taking $y=x$ gives $2\beta_d(x,x)=0$; the field $\Ql$ has characteristic $0$ [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero], so $2\neq0$ in $\Ql$ and $\beta_d(x,x)=0$ for all $x$: $\beta_d$ is a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form on the finite-dimensional $\Ql$-vector space $V_d$ (Step 1), over a field of characteristic $\neq2$. By [lem-weil-alternating-form-dimension], $\dim_{\Ql}V_d$ is even, and $b_d=\dim_{\Ql}V_d$ (Step 1) is even.

source.place: ## Proof, step 4 ('the symmetry clause of [prop-poincare-pairing] makes the pairing $(-1)^d$-symmetric. If $d$ is odd, choose a nonzero $\Ql$-linear trivialization $\Ql(-d)\simeq\Ql$ ... a nondegenerate alternating $\Ql$-valued form on $V_d$ ... characteristic is not $2$. Applying [lem-weil-alternating-form-dimension] gives $\dim V_d$ even'); the passage from $(-1)$-symmetric to alternating, which the blueprint skips, is written out. Milne, Remark 27.13, p. 159, uses the parity of the multiplicity of $q^{d/2}$ on $H^d$ instead and does not state this claim

proof_origin.place: ## Proof (steps 1-4 of the blueprint, rewritten as six steps; steps 2 and 3 follow Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Chapter II, §27, proof of Theorem 27.12, p. 158, with Remark 27.4(a), p. 155, as the per-step sources record; the remaining claims, $D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i}$, the Laurent identity and the parity of $b_d$, are the blueprint's and have no source in literature/ beyond it)

split_report.summary: Statement checked against the master blueprint file and the slopmaster2 LaTeX (01_final_weil_conjectures.tex, prop:duality-reciprocity, lines 3453-3482): same claims, kept verbatim. The statement leaves 'Frobenius eigenvalues in degree i, with algebraic multiplicity' undefined; the proof (Step 1) reads it as the multiset of reciprocal roots of P_{i,ell} in the chosen algebraic closure Qlb [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], which [prop-weil-reciprocal-roots-eigenvalues] identifies with the eigenvalues of F_{i,ell} after scalar extension; def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots was added to stmt_deps for that reason, and the Laurent ring Q[T,T^{-1}] and the substitution T -> q^{-d}T^{-1}, used without definition, now point to def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring (new) and def-weil-rational-function-field. stmt_deps completed with the notions the statement names (geometric hypotheses, global geometric Frobenius, cohomological family, coefficientwise extension, integral factor, Betti numbers, coefficient notation, determinant constants, trace-cup pairing). The four imported steps were replaced by six: the blueprint's step 1 asserted without argument that the transported operator q^d(F^{-1})^vee has eigenvalue multiset {q^d/alpha}, and its steps 2-3 computed with the factorization over an unnamed algebraic closure and never descended to Z or Q[T,T^{-1}]; the hidden linear algebra is now lem-weil-similitude-pairing-reciprocity (new), the polynomial computation is lem-weil-reciprocal-roots-laurent-identity (new), the factorization is the existing lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization, b_i = dim V_i is taken from prop-integral-recovery, D_i = det F_i from def-weil-determinant-constants, and the descents use lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero and lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective/-degree. The dependencies def-coefficient-twists-detailed and def-weil-finite-field-fiber, cited by the import in step 4, are kept where they are used (trivialization of Ql(-d) in Step 2; Qlb in Step 1). Both new lemmas are stated to match sorry-free Lean of slopmaster2 (WeilConjectures.ZetaLinearAlgebra.Pairing; WeilConjectures.Mathlib.FieldTheory.IsAlgClosed.Basic), recorded in their source fields; the proposition's own trace-datum form is WeilConjectures.ZetaLinearAlgebra.Reciprocity (reported as attachments).
